name: Alexei Navalny
milestone_by_age_26: No material milestone by age 26; graduated law in 1998 (age 22), worked as a corporate lawyer, and joined the Yabloko party in 2000, but his anti-corruption activism and national prominence arrived with the 2011 protests and beyond.
early_history_summary: Navalny grew up in Obninsk, graduated from Peoples' Friendship University with a law degree in 1998, and began working as a corporate lawyer. He joined the Yabloko political party around 2000 and was elected to the regional council of its Moscow branch in 2002, but his nationally significant activism came years later.
family_context_summary: Born to a Ukrainian father and Russian mother in Butyn, Moscow Oblast; father was from a village relocated after Chernobyl. Family was middle-class; no documented political or financial privilege.
evidence_summary: Navalny graduated law at 22 and joined Yabloko at 24, but his nationally significant anti-corruption activism and political fame did not materialize until the 2011 parliamentary election protests, when he was 35. No material, independently verifiable milestone by age 26 was found.

name: Stefan Bellof
milestone_by_age_26: Set the legendary Nürburgring Nordschleife lap record of 6:11.13 during qualifying for the 1000 km race in May 1983 at age 25, a record that stood for 35 years; also won the 1000 km Silverstone race that same season driving for the factory Porsche team.
early_history_summary: Bellof began karting at age 16 in 1973, following his older brother Georg. He won the German Karting Championship in 1980 and the Formula Ford 1600cc championship the same year, then moved into Formula Two and sportscar racing, joining the factory Rothmans Porsche team in 1983 where he immediately set historic lap times and won races.
family_context_summary: Born in Gießen, West Germany; followed his older brother Georg into karting. Family background beyond the brother's racing involvement is not documented in reviewed sources.
primary_early_advantage_tags: older sibling in motorsport, karting from 16, Porsche factory team access, German motorsport ecosystem
evidence_summary: Bellof began karting at 16 following his brother Georg, won the German Karting Championship at 22, and progressed rapidly through Formula Ford and Formula Two. In 1983, at age 25, he joined the factory Porsche sportscar team and set the legendary Nürburgring Nordschleife lap record of 6:11.13 that stood for 35 years. His older brother's racing involvement provided early domain exposure, and the Porsche factory team gave him elite-level equipment and teammates.
starting_point: Born in Gießen, West Germany; followed older brother Georg into karting; family background otherwise not documented in reviewed sources.
current_position: Died on 1 September 1985 at age 27 in a racing accident at Spa-Francorchamps, Belgium; final role: Formula One and sportscar driver for Tyrrell and Porsche.

trajectory.event: Made karting debut in the Automobilclub von Deutschland Federal Junior Cup.
Won the German Karting Championship and the Formula Ford 1600cc championship.
Set the legendary Nürburgring Nordschleife lap record of 6:11.13 in qualifying for the 1000 km race, driving a Porsche 956.
Won the FIA World Endurance Championship Drivers' title driving for the factory Rothmans Porsche team.
Made his Formula One debut with Tyrrell Racing at the Brazilian Grand Prix.
Killed in a racing accident during the 1000 km of Spa at Spa-Francorchamps, Belgium.

name: Ernst Hinterseer
milestone_by_age_26: Won the Austrian national championship in giant slalom in 1954 at age 22, and placed sixth in giant slalom at the 1956 Winter Olympics at age 24, establishing himself as a top-tier international competitor.
early_history_summary: Hinterseer grew up in Kitzbühel in a farmer's family, apprenticed as a carpenter after World War II, but focused on skiing. His first major win came at Wendelstein in 1953, followed by the 1954 Austrian giant slalom title, which earned him a spot on the Austrian team for the 1954 World Championships and the 1956 Olympic team.
family_context_summary: Born in a farmer's family in Kitzbühel, Austria; apprenticed as a carpenter after WWII but focused on skiing after finishing school.
parent_family_domain_summary: Not documented in reviewed sources; family was farming background with no documented skiing lineage.
primary_early_advantage_tags: Kitzbühel ski town, Kitzbüheler Ski Club, Austrian national team pipeline, farmer's son
evidence_summary: Hinterseer grew up in Kitzbühel, one of the world's premier skiing towns, and was a member of the Kitzbüheler Ski Club. Despite a farmer's background and a carpentry apprenticeship, he leveraged the local skiing infrastructure to win the 1954 Austrian giant slalom title at 22 and compete at the 1956 Olympics. The Kitzbühel ecosystem and Austrian national team pipeline were key advantages.
starting_point: Born to a farmer's family in Kitzbühel, Austria; apprenticed as a carpenter after World War II but focused on skiing.
current_position: Retired alpine skier; lives in Kitzbühel at age 94; won 1960 Olympic gold in slalom and bronze in giant slalom, later coached the Austrian Ski Federation.

trajectory.event: Achieved his first major win at Wendelstein, establishing himself as a competitive skier.
Won the Austrian national championship in giant slalom and was named to the Austrian team for the World Championships in Åre, Sweden.
Competed at the Cortina d'Ampezzo Winter Olympics, placing sixth in giant slalom.
Won Olympic gold in slalom and bronze in giant slalom at Squaw Valley, becoming Austrian Sportsman of the Year.
Won the world professional skiing title on the US pro circuit.
Retired from competition to become a coach, later heading the Austrian Ski Federation from 1974 to 1976.

name: Benny Hinn
milestone_by_age_26: No material milestone by age 26; Hinn emigrated to Toronto as a teenager, did not finish high school, and founded the Orlando Christian Center in 1983 at age 31, with his first nationally televised service in 1989.
early_history_summary: Hinn was born in Jaffa, Israel, to a family of Greek, Palestinian, and Armenian heritage, and emigrated to Toronto in 1968 after the Six-Day War. He attended Georges Vanier Secondary School but did not graduate, and experienced a religious conversion as a young man before eventually moving to the United States to found his ministry in 1983.
family_context_summary: Born in Jaffa, Israel, to parents of Greek, Palestinian, and Armenian heritage; family emigrated to Toronto in 1968. Hinn falsely claimed his father was mayor of Jaffa.
evidence_summary: Hinn's ministry career began in earnest with the founding of the Orlando Christian Center in 1983 at age 31, well after age 26. His first nationally televised Miracle Crusade was in 1989, and his television program This Is Your Day launched in 1990. No material, independently verifiable milestone by age 26 was found.

name: Brian Kernighan
milestone_by_age_26: No material milestone by age 26; Kernighan earned his bachelor's in engineering physics from the University of Toronto in 1964 and was a PhD student at Princeton through 1968, completing his doctorate in 1969 at age 27. His seminal contributions to Unix, AWK, and K&R C came later at Bell Labs.
early_history_summary: Kernighan studied engineering physics at the University of Toronto from 1960 to 1964, then pursued a PhD in electrical engineering at Princeton, completing his dissertation on graph partitioning problems in 1969. His career-defining work at Bell Labs on Unix, AWK, and The C Programming Language began after his doctorate.
family_context_summary: Born in Toronto, Ontario, Canada. Family background not documented in reviewed sources.
evidence_summary: Kernighan was a PhD student at Princeton through age 26, with his doctorate completed in 1969 at age 27. His landmark contributions — coining the term Unix, co-authoring The C Programming Language, and co-creating AWK — all came during his years at Bell Labs after 1969. No material, independently verifiable milestone by age 26 was found.

name: Joe Simpson
milestone_by_age_26: Made the first ascent of the previously unclimbed west face of Siula Grande (6,344 m) in the Cordillera Huayhuash of Peru in 1985 at age 25, a major mountaineering achievement that became legendary after his survival story was published in Touching the Void.
early_history_summary: Simpson was born in Kuala Lumpur to a Scottish father in the British Army and an Irish mother, and traveled between schools in Britain and various countries. He began rock climbing at age 14 after being introduced to the sport by a teacher at Ampleforth College, and was inspired by Heinrich Harrer's The White Spider. By his mid-twenties he was an experienced alpine climber attempting major first ascents in the Andes.
family_context_summary: Born in Kuala Lumpur to a Scottish father stationed with the British Army and an Irish mother; traveled between schools in Britain and countries where his father was posted. Attended Ampleforth College, a boarding school in Yorkshire.
parent_family_domain_summary: Father was a British Army officer; no documented mountaineering background in the family. A teacher at Ampleforth College introduced Simpson to climbing.
primary_early_advantage_tags: boarding school climbing intro, climbing partner Simon Yates, alpine experience, British mountaineering tradition
evidence_summary: Simpson was introduced to climbing at age 14 by a teacher at Ampleforth College and was inspired by The White Spider. By 25, he was an experienced alpine climber who, with partner Simon Yates, completed the first ascent of the west face of Siula Grande in Peru. The high-trust climbing partnership with Yates and years of alpine experience were critical to the achievement. The survival story from this climb became the bestseller Touching the Void.
starting_point: Born in Kuala Lumpur to a Scottish British Army father and an Irish mother; traveled between schools in Britain and various countries where his father was stationed.
current_position: British mountaineer and author; best known for Touching the Void (1988), which sold nearly two million copies and was adapted into a 2003 documentary film; continues as a motivational speaker and author.

trajectory.event: Introduced to rock climbing at Peak Scar in Yorkshire by a teacher at Ampleforth College.
Made the first ascent of the west face of Siula Grande (6,344 m) in Peru with Simon Yates; survived a broken leg and crevasse fall during the descent.
Published Touching the Void, which became a bestseller translated into 23 languages and selling nearly two million copies.
Touching the Void was adapted into an acclaimed documentary film.
The Beckoning Silence won the National Outdoor Book Award and was adapted into a Channel 4 documentary.

name: Rudolf E. Kálmán
milestone_by_age_26: No material milestone by age 26; Kálmán earned his SB (1953) and SM (1954) from MIT and was appointed Instructor in Control Theory at Columbia in 1955, but his seminal work — the Kalman filter — was published in 1960 at age 30, and his doctorate was completed in 1957 at age 27.
early_history_summary: Kálmán emigrated from Budapest to the United States in 1943, earned his bachelor's and master's degrees in electrical engineering from MIT in 1953 and 1954, and then went to Columbia University for doctoral work under John Ragazzini. He was appointed Instructor in Control Theory at Columbia in 1955 but his groundbreaking Kalman filter paper came in 1960.
family_context_summary: Born in Budapest, Hungary, in 1930 to Otto and Ursula Kálmán (née Grundmann); family emigrated to the United States in 1943. No further family background documented in reviewed sources.
evidence_summary: Kálmán was an instructor at Columbia University by age 25 but had not yet completed his doctorate (1957) or published his seminal Kalman filter paper (1960). His career-defining contributions came after age 26. No material, independently verifiable milestone by age 26 was found; his academic appointment was a standard early-career position, not a notable achievement.

name: Yoshitaka Amano
milestone_by_age_26: Served as character designer for iconic anime series including Gatchaman (1972–1974), Tekkaman, and Casshern at Tatsunoko Production, becoming one of the most influential character designers in Japanese anime by his early twenties.
early_history_summary: Amano was born in Shizuoka, Japan, the youngest of four children. His father was a traditional Suruga lacquerware artist. At age 15 in 1967, Amano joined Tatsunoko Production, where he began working on Speed Racer and was quickly promoted to character designer and animation director by age 17 or 18. He went on to design characters for Gatchaman, Tekkaman, Honeybee Hutch, and Casshern, remaining at Tatsunoko until going freelance in 1982.
family_context_summary: Born in Shizuoka, Japan, the youngest of four children. Father Yoshio (1917–1962) was a traditional Suruga lacquerware artist who died when Amano was 10. Family was not wealthy; Amano moved to a company dormitory in Tokyo at 15.
parent_family_domain_summary: Father was a traditional Suruga lacquerware artist, providing early exposure to visual art and craft traditions, though he died when Amano was young.
primary_early_advantage_tags: father lacquer artist, Tatsunoko Production at 15, anime industry frontier, Tokyo creative ecosystem, early character design role
evidence_summary: Amano's father was a traditional lacquerware artist, providing early art exposure. At 15, Amano boldly walked into Tatsunoko Production in Tokyo and was hired on the spot, moving into a company dormitory. By 17–18 he was a character designer and animation director, creating iconic characters for Gatchaman, Tekkaman, and Casshern. He was embedded in the early Japanese anime industry at a formative moment, accumulating over a decade of professional experience by age 26.
starting_point: Born in Shizuoka, Japan, the youngest of four children; father was a traditional Suruga lacquerware artist who died when Amano was 10; family was not wealthy.
current_position: Japanese visual artist and illustrator; operates Studio Devaloka; best known for character designs for Final Fantasy, Vampire Hunter D, and Gatchaman; five-time Seiun Award winner; active as of 2025.

trajectory.event: Joined Tatsunoko Production in Tokyo, beginning his career in animation on Speed Racer.
Served as character designer for Gatchaman, one of the most influential anime series of the era.
Left Tatsunoko Production to become a freelance artist, illustrating The Guin Saga and Vampire Hunter D novels.
Commissioned to create character designs and illustrations for the Final Fantasy video game franchise, beginning a long-term collaboration.
Won the Bram Stoker Award for Sandman: The Dream Hunters, a collaboration with Neil Gaiman.
Established Studio Devaloka, a film production company.

name: Bob Ross
milestone_by_age_26: No material milestone by age 26; Ross enlisted in the US Air Force in 1961 at age 18 and was serving as a medical records technician through his twenties. His painting career and television show The Joy of Painting did not begin until 1983, when he was 41.
early_history_summary: Ross was born in Daytona Beach, Florida, dropped out of high school in the 9th grade, and worked as a carpenter with his father before enlisting in the Air Force in 1961. He developed an interest in painting during his military service after attending a USO art class in Anchorage, but his public painting career only emerged after his retirement from the military in 1981.
family_context_summary: Born in Daytona Beach, Florida; father Jack was a carpenter and mother Ollie was a waitress. Ross dropped out of high school in the 9th grade and worked as a carpenter with his father before enlisting in the Air Force.
parent_family_domain_summary: Father was a carpenter; no documented art background in the family.
evidence_summary: Ross was a US Air Force enlisted man throughout his twenties, serving as a medical records technician and first sergeant. He discovered painting during his military service but did not launch his public painting career or television show until after retiring from the Air Force in 1981 at age 39. The Joy of Painting began airing in 1983 when Ross was 41. No material, independently verifiable milestone by age 26 was found.

name: Egberto Gismonti
milestone_by_age_26: Released his self-titled debut album in 1969 at age 22 on Elenco Records, followed by multiple albums through 1973 including Água e Vinho (1972) and Árvore (1973), establishing a recording career that blended classical training with Brazilian popular music.
early_history_summary: Gismonti was born in Carmo, Rio de Janeiro, into a musical family of Sicilian and Lebanese heritage. He began studying piano at age 6 at the Brazilian Conservatory of Music, studied classical repertoire for 15 years, then went to Paris to study with Nadia Boulanger and Jean Barraqué. Boulanger encouraged him to incorporate Brazilian experience into his music, leading directly to his first album in 1969.
family_context_summary: Born into a musical family in Carmo, Rio de Janeiro; mother was from Sicily and father from Beirut, Lebanon. Grandfather and uncle Edgar were responsible for the town's band. Family provided early musical immersion.
parent_family_domain_summary: Musical family: grandfather and uncle ran the town band in Carmo; mother Sicilian, father Lebanese, providing a multicultural musical environment.
primary_early_advantage_tags: musical family, piano from age 6, Brazilian Conservatory, Nadia Boulanger in Paris, classical and popular fusion
evidence_summary: Gismonti began piano studies at age 6 at the Brazilian Conservatory of Music, accumulating 15 years of classical training before going to Paris to study with Nadia Boulanger and Jean Barraqué. Boulanger's mentorship redirected him toward Brazilian popular music, leading to his debut album in 1969 at age 22. His musical family (grandfather and uncle ran the town band) and elite conservatory training provided deep technical foundations and mentorship.
starting_point: Born into a musical family in Carmo, Rio de Janeiro, Brazil; mother from Sicily, father from Beirut; grandfather and uncle ran the town band.
current_position: Brazilian composer, pianist, and guitarist; active recording and performing artist spanning five decades; founded the Carmo music label in 1978; continues to perform internationally as of 2025.

trajectory.event: Began studying piano at the Brazilian Conservatory of Music.
His composition O Sonho was performed at the III Festival Internacional da Canção in Rio with his arrangement for a 100-piece orchestra.
Released his self-titled debut album on Elenco Records, launching his recording career.
Released Água e Vinho on EMI-Odeon, further establishing his distinctive fusion of classical and Brazilian popular music.
Released Dança das Cabeças on ECM with Naná Vasconcelos, nominated Album of the Year by Stereo Review and winner of the Großer Deutscher Schallplattenpreis.
Founded the Carmo music label, with several joint ventures with ECM.

name: Yevgeny Kafelnikov
milestone_by_age_26: Won the 1996 French Open singles title at age 22, becoming the first Russian to win a Grand Slam singles title, and also won the doubles title that year; reached world No. 1 in May 1999 at age 25 and won the 1999 Australian Open.
early_history_summary: Kafelnikov was born in Sochi, Russia, and turned professional in 1992 at age 18. His breakthrough came in 1994 when he won three ATP titles and rose from rank 102 to year-end 11. By 1995 he reached his first Grand Slam semifinal, and in 1996 he won the French Open, becoming the first Russian Grand Slam champion in history.
family_context_summary: Born in Sochi, Russian SFSR, Soviet Union. Family background and early tennis training not documented in reviewed sources beyond his birthplace.
primary_early_advantage_tags: turned pro at 18, Sochi sports town, coach Lepeshin, ATP tour early, Russian tennis post-Soviet opening
evidence_summary: Kafelnikov turned professional at 18 in 1992 and rose rapidly, winning three ATP titles in 1994 and reaching his first Grand Slam semifinal in 1995. At 22, he won the 1996 French Open, becoming the first Russian Grand Slam singles champion. His coach Lepeshin played a key role, believing in Kafelnikov when others did not. The post-Soviet opening of Russian tennis provided a structural opportunity. He reached world No. 1 in 1999 and won Olympic gold in 2000, all by age 26.
starting_point: Born in Sochi, Russian SFSR, Soviet Union; family background not documented in reviewed sources.
current_position: Retired Russian tennis player; inducted into the International Tennis Hall of Fame in 2019; career prize money of approximately $23.9 million; resides in Sochi, Russia.

trajectory.event: Turned professional on the ATP Tour.
Won three ATP titles and rose from rank 102 to year-end 11, establishing himself as a top player.
Won the French Open singles and doubles titles, becoming the first Russian to win a Grand Slam singles championship.
Won the Australian Open singles title and reached the world No. 1 ranking on 3 May 1999.
Won the Olympic gold medal in men's singles at the Sydney Olympics.
Inducted into the International Tennis Hall of Fame.

name: Chris Froome
milestone_by_age_26: Finished second overall in the 2011 Vuelta a España at age 26 (later retrospectively promoted to first), matching the best-ever Grand Tour result for a British rider and winning stage 17 at Peña Cabarga; this was a breakthrough Grand Tour performance.
early_history_summary: Froome was born in Nairobi, Kenya, to British-origin parents, and grew up in Kenya and South Africa. He began cycling at 13, mentored by professional cyclist David Kinjah in Kenya, and attended school in Bloemfontein, South Africa, where he was cycling captain. He turned professional at 22 with Team Konica Minolta in 2007, joined Barloworld in 2008, and moved to Team Sky in 2010, where his 2011 Vuelta breakthrough came as a domestique.
family_context_summary: Born in Nairobi, Kenya, to English father Clive (a former field hockey player who represented England at under-19 level) and Kenyan-born mother Jane of British origin. Youngest of three boys; brothers attended Rugby School in England. Parents maintained British customs at home.
parent_family_domain_summary: Father was a former field hockey player who represented England at under-19 level; mother was born and raised in Kenya to British parents who emigrated to run a crop farm. Sporting family background but not cycling-specific.
primary_early_advantage_tags: mentor David Kinjah, British-South African schooling, Team Sky pipeline, late specialization, British cycling infrastructure
evidence_summary: Froome grew up in Kenya with British-origin parents and was mentored by professional cyclist David Kinjah from age 13. He moved to South Africa for schooling, where he was cycling captain at St John's College. He turned professional relatively late at 22, and his breakthrough came at 26 with second overall in the 2011 Vuelta a España. His father's sporting background (England under-19 field hockey) and the mentorship of Kinjah were documented advantages, though his path was unconventional and his Grand Tour potential was not recognized until 2011.
starting_point: Born in Nairobi, Kenya, to British-origin parents; father a former England under-19 field hockey player, mother Kenyan-born of British heritage; grew up in Kenya and South Africa.
current_position: British road racing cyclist; four-time Tour de France winner (2013, 2015, 2016, 2017), Giro d'Italia winner (2018), and two-time Vuelta a España winner (2011, 2017); rode for Israel–Premier Tech; largely inactive due to injuries from a 2019 crash.

trajectory.event: Introduced to organized cycling by his mother in Kenya and met mentor David Kinjah.
Turned professional with Team Konica Minolta in South Africa.
Finished second overall in the Vuelta a España (later retrospectively promoted to first), a breakthrough Grand Tour performance; also won stage 17 at Peña Cabarga.
Won his first Tour de France, the first British rider to do so since 2012.
Won his second Tour de France and the mountains classification.
Won his fourth Tour de France followed by the Vuelta a España, completing the Tour-Vuelta double.
Won the Giro d'Italia, holding all three Grand Tour winners' jerseys simultaneously.
